# Scanpath Studio

> Free, open-source software for visualizing eye-tracking data from reading studies: scanpaths, fixations, saccades, gaze heatmaps and raw gaze drawn over the text, from EyeLink, Tobii and other eye trackers.

Scanpath Studio is an interactive Streamlit workbench, a Python API (`import scanpath_studio as sps`) and a CLI (`scanpath-studio`) for eye-tracking-while-reading data: it draws fixations, saccades and heatmaps over the text at its true on-screen position, shows the per-word reading measures your data brings (FFD, FPRT, RPD, TFD, skips, regressions), compares participants, and exports figures and tables. The bundled demo is a subset of the OneStop Eye Movements corpus.

# Use the app

# Get started

## Install

- **Desktop app** Recommended

  No coding required. Your data stays on your computer.

  [macOS](https://github.com/lacclab/scanpath-studio/releases/latest/download/ScanpathStudio-macos-arm64.dmg) [Windows](https://github.com/lacclab/scanpath-studio/releases/latest/download/ScanpathStudio-windows-x86_64-setup.exe) [Linux](https://github.com/lacclab/scanpath-studio/releases/latest/download/ScanpathStudio-linux-x86_64.tar.gz)

  Setup details & other downloads

  - macOS 14+, Apple silicon: open the DMG, drag to Applications, then launch. If blocked: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway. Intel Mac or older macOS? Use Python below.
  - Windows: run the installer, then launch from Start. If SmartScreen warns: More info → Run anyway. A [portable ZIP](https://github.com/lacclab/scanpath-studio/releases/latest/download/ScanpathStudio-windows-x86_64.zip) is also available.
  - Linux: extract, then run `./ScanpathStudio/ScanpathStudio`.

  [All downloads](https://github.com/lacclab/scanpath-studio/releases/latest)

- **Try online**

  Explore the bundled demo. No installation.

  [Launch demo](https://scanpath-studio.streamlit.app)

- **Install with Python**

  Python 3.11–3.14. Opens in your browser.

  ```
  pip install scanpath-studio
  scanpath-studio
  ```

## Your first figure

Start with the bundled demo, a subset of the [OneStop corpus](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/loading-data/#onestop). You don't need to prepare any files. Choose a look, then save an interactive figure.

\[!\[

\](../assets/workflows/design-presets_poster.webp)\](../assets/workflows/design-presets.mp4)

- **1 · Open a reading**

  In the **Scanpath** view, choose **Bundled demo** in **Select dataset**. Then choose a reading in **Select trial**.

- **2 · Choose a view**

  In **Design presets**, click **Heatmap** to see where fixation time concentrates. Click **Scanpath** to follow the order of fixations.

- **3 · Save your figure**

  In the **Export** tab under the plot, find **Current figure**. Set **Download format** to **HTML**, then click **⬇ Download HTML**. Open the saved file in your browser to zoom and hover over the figure.

## Next steps

- **[Bring your own data](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/loading-data/#add-your-own-data)**

  Import your recordings and check the column mapping.

- **[Prepare a figure](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/exporting-figures/export-one-figure/index.md)**

  Choose a format and size for your paper or slides.

- **[Explore more views](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/gallery/index.md)**

  Try an example, then follow its app instructions or the [feature guides](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/index.md).

- **[Work in code](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/scanpath-visualization/#render-in-code)**

  Reproduce a view in Python or with the CLI.

# Analyze a corpus

- **[Analyze one text](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/corpus-analysis/analyze-one-text/index.md)**

  Compare word-by-word measures across participants.

- **[Compare groups or conditions](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/corpus-analysis/compare-groups/index.md)**

  Inspect group means and differences.

- **[See progression over time](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/corpus-analysis/progression-over-time/index.md)**

  Inspect trends within or across trials.

## Before you start

Open a dataset and set the trial filters for your question. Word-level views need [reading measures in the Words table](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/loading-data/#reading-measures); the bundled demo includes them. To compare participants on one text, their trials of that text must share one text ID.

## Keep the result

**⬇ Download this table (CSV)** saves the values. **⬇ Download the recipe (JSON)** saves the dataset name, the trial filters, the analysis choices and the counts. The recipe names the dataset but holds none of its data, so keep the source data to reproduce the result.

To draw a summary with Python or the CLI, see [Plot a summary in code](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/corpus-workspace/#plot-a-summary-in-code).

# Analyze one text

Compare how participants read the words of one text.

1. [Select the trials](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/corpus-analysis/#before-you-start), then open **Corpus Analysis** → **Per text**.
1. Pick a text and a reading measure your data provides.
1. In **View**, choose **Measure on the stimulus**. To plot the measure against a word feature such as surprisal, choose **Measure vs feature** and pick the **Feature**. Your Words table must have that column.
1. In **Aggregate**, choose how the values are combined. **Cohort profile** also draws a **Spread** band, and its **Min participants per word** leaves out words that too few participants have a value for.
1. [Download the table and recipe](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/corpus-analysis/#keep-the-result).

\[!\[

\](../../../assets/workflows/corpus-analysis_poster.webp)\](../../../assets/workflows/corpus-analysis.mp4)

*The recording shows total fixation duration on a text, against GPT-2 surprisal, and between two groups.*

# Compare groups or conditions

Compare a reading measure between two groups of participants or two conditions.

1. [Select the trials](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/corpus-analysis/#before-you-start), then open **Corpus Analysis** → **Groups**.
1. Turn on **Compare a second group**.
1. Choose **Split a field** to form the groups from the values of one column, or **Independent filter sets** to define each group by a separate set of filters.
1. In **View**, choose **Group means & difference** and a measure. Check the number of participants in each group and whether any participant is in both. The **Standardized difference** (Cohen's d) is shown only when the groups share no participant.
1. [Download the table and recipe](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/corpus-analysis/#keep-the-result).

The comparison is descriptive. It runs no significance test. For a recorded example, see [Analyze one text](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/corpus-analysis/analyze-one-text/index.md).

# See progression over time

Inspect a measure within trials or across a session.

1. [Select the trials](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/corpus-analysis/#before-you-start) and open **Corpus Analysis**.

1. Choose the view for the question:

   | Scope                                                       | View                                                  |
   | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
   | One participant across trials                               | **Per participant** → **Per-trial trend**             |
   | Fixation duration within trials, pooled for one participant | **Per participant** → **Fixation duration over time** |
   | A group across trials                                       | **Groups** → **Group trend**                          |

1. Choose a measure, and an **Aggregate** where the view offers one. Across-trial trends order each participant's trials by a `trial_index` or `TRIAL_INDEX` column. Without one, the app orders them by fixation time, or as listed, and this may differ from the order the trials were shown. For the within-trial view, set **X axis** to **Fixation order**, or to **Time (ms)** when the data records fixation onsets.

1. [Download the table and recipe](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/corpus-analysis/#keep-the-result).

# Optimize data collection

- **[Check a session](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-collection/check-a-session/index.md)**

  Inspect a pilot or completed recording.

- **[Compare two eye trackers](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-collection/compare-eye-trackers/index.md)**

  Review recordings of the same text.

- **[Audit an experimenter](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-collection/audit-an-experimenter/index.md)**

  Review sessions by who collected them.

Start with a [loaded dataset](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/loading-data/#add-your-own-data). To apply exclusion decisions after reviewing, use [Filter data](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-filtering/index.md).

# Audit an experimenter

Review recordings collected by one experimenter.

1. Keep the experimenter column when you import the data, under **Extra fields to keep**. If each participant had one experimenter, you can instead attach it in a participant metadata table.
1. Open the filter () beside **Select trial** and choose the experimenter. Columns of a participant metadata table are under **By participant**.
1. [Inspect and replay their trials](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-collection/check-a-session/#2-inspect-a-trial).
1. In **Annotations**, tag trials `review` and note recurring problems.
1. [Export the review](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-collection/check-a-session/#5-save-the-review).

To compare experimenters, turn on **Compare**. Use the filter on each scanpath's row to pick a different experimenter, and choose readings of the same text.

# Check a session

Inspect a recording and save the trials that need attention.

## 1. Open the session

[Import your tables](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/loading-data/#add-your-own-data), or select a loaded dataset. Check that its **Recording setup** matches the screen used in the experiment.

## 2. Inspect a trial

In the **Scanpath** view, pick a trial in **Select trial**. Turn on **Word boxes** and check:

- whether the boxes match the stimulus image, if you have one;
- where the fixations sit relative to the words;
- unexpected gaps, shifts or off-screen positions.

For a consistent offset, check [coordinate units and screen setup](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/faq/#the-fixations-dont-line-up-with-the-text).

## 3. Replay the recording

Turn on **Animate** to follow the fixation order and timing. To mark short or long fixations, or fixations outside the text, open **Filters & highlights** ▾ → **Fixations** and set **Short**, **Long** or **Outside the text** to **Highlight**. A gap or an unusual scanpath does not tell you its cause.

\[!\[

\](../../../assets/workflows/replay_poster.webp)\](../../../assets/workflows/replay.mp4)

## 4. Record the review

In **Annotations**, tag the trial `review` and write what you observed in **Notes**. Use ◀ ▶ beside **Select trial** to move through the session.

## 5. Save the review

Export favorites, tags and notes from **Data Management** → **Annotations** → **Export**. The file includes participant and trial IDs. **Open** on an annotation row returns to that trial.

For exclusion decisions, follow [Exclude unsuitable trials](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-filtering/exclude-unsuitable-trials/index.md).

# Compare two eye trackers

Review the same text recorded with two trackers or setups.

1. [Import each recording](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/loading-data/#add-your-own-data) as a separate dataset, each with the **Recording setup** of its tracker.
1. Open the first dataset in the **Scanpath** view and pick a trial.
1. Turn on **Compare**. In scanpath B's row, choose the second dataset in **Dataset B** and a trial of the same text in **Trial B**.
1. Compare fixation placement, spread and missing stretches. An overlay needs both datasets recorded on the same screen size. Otherwise the app shows the two scanpaths side by side.

\[!\[

\](../../../assets/workflows/compare_poster.webp)\](../../../assets/workflows/compare.mp4)

*This recording compares two participants in the bundled demo. For two trackers, choose the second recording in **Dataset B**.*

Use [the session-review steps](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-collection/check-a-session/#4-record-the-review) to save observations.

# Filter data

- **[Exclude unsuitable trials](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-filtering/exclude-unsuitable-trials/index.md)**

  Leave tagged trials out.

- **[Select participants by a field](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-filtering/select-participants/index.md)**

  Use participant metadata.

- **[Find the trials an analysis needs](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-filtering/find-trials-for-an-analysis/index.md)**

  Select trials after inspecting fixations.

## Before you start

Open a dataset in the **Scanpath** view. The filter () beside **Select trial** selects whole trials. **Filters & highlights** in the Plot controls changes which fixations and saccades the figure draws.

\[!\[

\](../../assets/workflows/trial-filtering_poster.webp)\](../../assets/workflows/trial-filtering.mp4)

## Check and export the selection

1. Check the remaining trial and participant counts and inspect a few trials.
1. Follow [Export every trial](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/exporting-figures/export-every-trial/index.md) and choose **All filtered trials**. The bundle's `index.csv` lists its files with their participant and trial IDs.
1. Keep a full decision record with [Data Management → Annotations → Export](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-collection/check-a-session/#5-save-the-review). The annotations in a bundle cover only the exported trials.

# Exclude unsuitable trials

Apply your exclusion criteria and leave rejected trials out of the selection.

1. [Review the session](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-collection/check-a-session/#2-inspect-a-trial). Judge each trial against your study's criteria. A scanpath pattern alone does not establish skimming or poor calibration.
1. In **Annotations**, tag rejected trials `exclude` and write a short reason in **Notes**.
1. Open the filter () beside **Select trial**. Under **By trial annotation**, add `exclude` to **Excluding tags**.
1. [Check and export the selection](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-filtering/#every-task-ends-the-same-way).

For a trial with several screens, tag the whole trial. A tag on one screen does not exclude the trial.

\[!\[

\](../../../assets/workflows/favorites_poster.webp)\](../../../assets/workflows/favorites.mp4)

*The recording shows favorites and tags. For the selection above, use the `exclude` tag and **Excluding tags**.*

# Find the trials an analysis needs

Locate trials containing particular fixation patterns.

1. Open **Filters & highlights** ▾ → **Fixations**.

1. Set the **Mode** of the category you need to **Highlight**:

   - **Short** or **Long**, with a duration threshold in **ms**
   - **Outside the text**, for fixations in no word box
   - **Near a blink**, if your data has a blink column

1. Step through the trials. In **Annotations**, tag those that meet your analysis criteria, for example `include`.

1. Open the filter () beside **Select trial**. Under **By trial annotation**, add `include` to **With any of these tags**.

1. [Check and export the selection](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-filtering/#every-task-ends-the-same-way).

# Select participants by a field

Select participants using metadata such as native language, age or group.

1. Attach a participant metadata table, with one row per participant and a participant ID column. When you add a dataset, use **Metadata** → **Participants**. For a loaded dataset, use **Data Management** → **Edit dataset** → **Data tables & column mapping**.
1. Open the filter () beside **Select trial** and find **By participant**.
1. Choose a field and the values or range to keep.
1. Check the remaining participant IDs and [export the selection](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-filtering/#every-task-ends-the-same-way).

To also apply trial-level quality criteria, follow [Exclude unsuitable trials](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/data-filtering/exclude-unsuitable-trials/index.md).

# Export customized figures

- **[Export one figure](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/exporting-figures/export-one-figure/index.md)**

  A static image or interactive HTML.

- **[Export a replay](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/exporting-figures/export-a-replay/index.md)**

  GIF, MP4 or interactive HTML.

- **[Export every trial](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/exporting-figures/export-every-trial/index.md)**

  A ZIP of figures and data tables.

For installation requirements or a failed export, see the [export FAQ](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/faq/#export-fails).

# Export a replay

Save an animated reading for a talk or supplement.

1. Pick a trial in the **Scanpath** view and turn on **Animate**.
1. In **Animate** ▾ → **Replay**, set the **Speed**. Turn on the layers you want to show.
1. Open the **Export** tab. Under **Current figure**, set **Download format** to **GIF**, **MP4** or **HTML**.
1. Download the replay. GIF and MP4 play at the selected speed. HTML keeps the interactive playback controls.

\[!\[

\](../../../assets/workflows/replay-export_poster.webp)\](../../../assets/workflows/replay-export.mp4)

*Exporting a GIF. The recording shortens the rendering wait.*

For [GIF/MP4 export from Python](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/exporting/#replays-as-gif-or-mp4), see Export and share.

# Export every trial

Build a ZIP of static figures and data tables for a set of trials.

1. [Set the figure's design](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/exporting-figures/export-one-figure/#1-choose-the-view) once. Each exported trial uses that design, without animation or a comparison partner.
1. Open the **Export** tab. Under **Export bundle** → **Trials to include**, choose **This trial**, **All filtered trials**, **All trials of one participant**, **All trials of one text** or **All trials, ignoring filters**.
1. Choose the **Figure formats** and, under **Also include**, the tables and their **Table format**. Check the **File path pattern**. To edit individual layers later, turn on **Layers as separate files**.
1. Click **Build export**, download the bundle, and inspect one exported figure.

\[!\[

\](../../../assets/workflows/export-bundle_poster.webp)\](../../../assets/workflows/export-bundle.mp4)

*Exporting figures and tables for the bundled demo's trials. The recording speeds up the build.*

Keep each trial's `plot_config.json` for the design, `README.md` for the build details and `index.csv` for the file list and failures. Keep your original data and record its version and the selected trial filters separately.

For a [scripted batch](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/exporting/#batch-pattern), use the Python recipe in Export and share.

# Export one figure

Save a scanpath, heatmap or comparison at the size you need.

## 1. Choose the view

Pick a trial in the **Scanpath** view. Choose one of the **Design presets**, or set the layers in the Plot controls. Turn on **Compare** if the figure needs two readings. Check that text and markers are readable and nothing is clipped.

## 2. Set the format and size

Open the **Export** tab and find **Current figure**. Choose the **Download format**:

| Output             | Format     |
| ------------------ | ---------- |
| Image              | PNG        |
| Vector figure      | SVG or PDF |
| Interactive figure | HTML       |

For a print PNG, set **Width** and **DPI**. For HTML that opens offline, tick **Self-contained HTML**.

## 3. Download

Click the download button for the chosen format, such as **⬇ Download PNG**.

\[!\[

\](../../../assets/workflows/export-figure_poster.webp)\](../../../assets/workflows/export-figure.mp4)

*Exporting a PNG at 180 mm and 300 dpi.*

## 4. Reuse the design or share the figure

- **My designs** in the Plot controls saves the look for other trials.
- **Share** → **Link** reopens the trial and its settings. The link does not carry data you uploaded, so load that data separately.
- [**Share** → **Code**](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/exporting/#from-the-app-to-a-script) gives Python or CLI code that redraws the figure.
- **Share** → **Settings file** → **Download settings** saves the settings, and **Restore settings** loads them again.

Each guide explains one part of the app, with Python and CLI examples where they apply. For step-by-step workflows, see the [tutorials](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/index.md).

  Layers, filters, replay, and comparison, also across two datasets.

  Built-in and public datasets, importing your files, column mapping and the recording setup.

- **[Corpus Analysis](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/corpus-workspace/index.md)**

  Per text, Per participant and Groups, from the reading measures in your data.

- **[Export and share](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/exporting/index.md)**

  Figure downloads, share links and code, batch export and replay export.

# Corpus Analysis

The **Corpus Analysis** view summarizes reading measures by text, participant or group. It uses the selected dataset and the trials your filters keep.

## Choose a view

Open a tab, then pick a figure in its **View** menu.

| Tab                 | Use it to                                                          |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Per text**        | Compare word-by-word reading across participants                   |
| **Per participant** | Inspect one participant across trials                              |
| **Groups**          | Describe a group of trials, or compare two, such as two conditions |

Choose the **Measure**, how to **Aggregate** it and, where a view draws a band, its **Spread**. For word profiles, set **Min participants per word**.

## Supply reading measures

Word-level views use the [reading measures in your data](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/loading-data/#reading-measures), such as first fixation duration or total fixation duration. Map those columns when you import. Views of single fixations, such as **Fixation duration over time**, use the Fixations table.

## Compare groups

Under **Define groups by**, choose **Split a field** to pick a group by the values of one field, or **Independent filter sets** to build it from filters. Turn on **Compare a second group** to define a group B and see the two groups side by side, their means and their difference. These views are descriptive and run no significance tests.

## Save results

Under each result, **⬇ Download this table (CSV)** saves the table and **⬇ Download the recipe (JSON)** saves how it was made: the dataset, the trial filters, the analysis choices and the counts. The recipe holds no data rows and no figure settings. To inspect single trials, return to the Scanpath view.

## Plot a summary in code

Start from a tidy summary table, such as a **Cohort profile** table downloaded from Corpus Analysis. A word profile needs `word_id` and `value` columns, with optional `lo` and `hi` for a band. The downloaded table names the word ID column as your data does, so rename it to `word_id` if needed. For a trend over trial order, see [Across the experiment](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/gallery/across-experiment/index.md).

Python and CLI: word profile

```
import pandas as pd
import scanpath_studio as sps

profile = pd.read_csv("profile.csv")
fig = sps.plot_corpus_figure(
    profile, kind="profile", measure_label="Total fixation duration (ms)"
)
sps.save_figure(fig, "profile.html")
```

```
scanpath-studio corpus --input profile.csv --kind profile \
  --measure-label "Total fixation duration (ms)" -o profile.html
```

[API parameters](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/api/#scanpath_studio.api.plot_corpus_figure) · [CLI options](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/cli/#corpus)

# Export and share

Save a figure, export many trials at once, or reuse a view in the app or in code.

## In the app

| Goal                                | Where                                            |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| Save the figure or replay on screen | **Export** → **Current figure**                  |
| Export many trials and their tables | **Export** → **Export bundle**                   |
| Share a view or copy its code       | **Share** → **Link** or **Code**                 |
| Reuse the figure settings           | **My designs**, or **Share** → **Settings file** |

For step-by-step instructions, see the [export tutorials](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/exporting-figures/index.md).

\[!\[

\](../../assets/workflows/share-link_poster.webp)\](../../assets/workflows/share-link.mp4)

A link reopens the trial and its settings for anyone who has the same dataset. [All controls → Under the plot](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/#under-the-plot) says what the recipient needs.

## Reproduce a figure

Open **Share** → **Code** and copy the Python or CLI code. It carries the figure's settings and your column mapping. For a dataset you imported, replace the placeholder file paths with your own. [Render in code](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/scanpath-visualization/#render-in-code) shows a minimal example.

For a PNG at print size, pass `width_mm` and `dpi` to `save_figure`, or `--width-mm` and `--dpi` to `render`. To edit the layers in a vector editor, save each layer to a separate file with `save_figure_layers` or `render --separable-layers`. In the app's export bundle, this is **Layers as separate files**.

## Batch export

In the app, **Export bundle** → **Trials to include** picks the trials: **This trial**, **All filtered trials**, **All trials of one participant**, **All trials of one text** or **All trials, ignoring filters**. For a scripted batch, loop over the trial list:

Python: one HTML figure per trial

```
from pathlib import Path

import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
out = Path("figures")
out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

for pid, tid in sps.list_trials(words, fixations).itertuples(index=False):
    fig = sps.plot_scanpath(words, fixations, pid, tid)
    sps.save_figure(fig, out / f"{pid}_{tid}.html")
```

Use the [data loaders](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/loading-data/#load-and-inspect-in-code) for your own files. The CLI's `render` writes one trial per run.

## Replay export

With **Animate** on, **Export** → **Current figure** saves the replay as HTML, GIF or MP4. The CLI's `render --animate` saves interactive HTML only. For a GIF or MP4 in Python:

Python: save a GIF or MP4

```
from pathlib import Path

import scanpath_studio as sps
from scanpath_studio.animation_export import export_animation

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
replay = sps.animate_scanpath(words, fixations, "l37_1129", "l37_1129_2_1_1_Ele")
Path("replay.mp4").write_bytes(export_animation(replay, fmt="mp4"))
```

Use `fmt="gif"` and a `.gif` filename for GIF output.

[Export setup and troubleshooting](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/faq/#export-fails) · [Python save options](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/api/#save) · [CLI options](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/cli/#common-tasks)

# Data Management

Load your own data, open a public dataset, or try the bundled demo.

## Choose a dataset

Pick a dataset in **Select dataset** above the plot, or in the dataset list on the **Data Management** page:

- **Bundled demo**: 24 trials from OneStop, with two participants and 12 texts.
- **Hand-drawn sample**: a scanpath drawn by hand over a short English text, which you can edit.
- Public datasets: OneStop and PoTeC. In the desktop app or a pip install, each downloads the first time you open it.
- **+** → **Import files**: your own tables.
- **+** → **Draw a scanpath**: write a text and place its fixations by hand.

### OneStop

The bundled demo comes from [OneStop Eye Movements](https://github.com/lacclab/OneStop-Eye-Movements) (Berzak et al., 2025), an English corpus with 360 participants. The full corpus is available as four public datasets: **OneStop · Ordinary reading**, **OneStop · Information seeking**, **OneStop · Repeated reading** and **OneStop · Information seeking (repeated)**. Each downloads once from [OSF](https://osf.io/2prdq/).

## What your data needs

A dataset needs at least one of the first three tables below. Add the others as you need them.

| Table                  | Contents                                                       |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Fixations              | One row per fixation: trial ID, duration, and x/y or a word ID |
| Words (interest areas) | One row per word: trial ID, word ID and word box               |
| Raw gaze               | One row per gaze sample: trial ID, x and y                     |
| Participants           | One row per participant, with metadata                         |
| Trials                 | One row per trial, with metadata                               |
| Texts                  | One row per text, with metadata                                |

The app detects columns from common eye-tracker exports. Check and correct the mapping when you import. To keep condition labels and other columns, pick them under **Extra fields to keep**. You can filter, sort and group trials by any metadata field.

### Files and units

- CSV, TSV, TXT, Parquet, Feather, Excel, or a ZIP of these files
- Positions in pixels
- Times in milliseconds. A time column whose header names its unit, such as `[s]`, `[μs]` or `[ns]`, is converted.
- Word boxes as `x/y/width/height` or EyeLink's `IA_LEFT/RIGHT/TOP/BOTTOM`

### Trials over several screens

Map the **Screen ID** field in your tables. A column named `screen_index` sets the order of the screens. Without one, the screens are ordered by where they first appear. The app draws one screen at a time.

### Reading measures

Corpus Analysis uses the per-word reading measures in your Words table, such as first fixation duration or total fixation duration. Map them when you import. EyeLink's `IA_*` columns are detected.

## Add your own data

1. Choose **+** → **Import files** and name the dataset.
1. Upload your tables and check the column mapping.
1. Under **Recording setup**, enter the **Screen**, **Monitor width** and **Text size** if you know them.
1. Optionally, in the desktop app or a local install, attach the stimulus images from a folder.
1. Click **Add dataset**, then **Open in Scanpath** to see its first trial. Later, **Open in Scanpath** beside **Add dataset** on the Data page does the same for the selected dataset.

\[!\[

\](../../assets/workflows/add-your-data_poster.webp)\](../../assets/workflows/add-your-data.mp4)

## Load and inspect in code

Load the same files in a script. The loaders detect column names the same way the app does.

Python and CLI

```
import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_scanpath_data("ia.csv", "fixations.csv")
print(sps.list_trials(words, fixations))
```

```
scanpath-studio render --words ia.csv --fixations fixations.csv --list-trials
scanpath-studio check --words ia.csv --fixations fixations.csv
```

For raw gaze, metadata and explicit column mappings, see the [loaders](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/api/#load-your-data) and [CLI input options](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/cli/#flags-input).

## Manage datasets

Click a dataset in the dataset list to open it. Below the list, **What's in *‹dataset›*** shows its tables, annotations and **Data checks**. When a check flags more than half of a table, such as every duration read as 0 ms, the Scanpath view says so above the plot.

Use **Edit dataset** to change its name, column mapping, recording setup or metadata, then click **Save changes**. **Download setup file** saves the mapping and recording setup, so you can apply them to similar data.

The editor offers only the columns kept when the dataset was added. To use a column that isn't listed, remove the dataset and add it again from its files, mapping the column or keeping it under **Extra fields to keep**.

# Scanpath visualization

1. Views and Help.
1. The trial control bar: dataset, trial, screen, sort (⇅) and filter ().
1. The trial's summary.
1. The figure.
1. Plot controls.
1. The tabs: Annotations, Stimulus & context, Comparisons, Export and Share.

The **Scanpath** view draws one reading at a time, at the size of the screen it was recorded on.

Looking for a specific button?

[All controls](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/index.md) lists every button and setting on this view, menu by menu, with a picture of each menu. Search it for what you want to change, such as *saccade color* or *legend position*.

## Choose a trial

Pick a trial in **Select trial** above the plot, or step through the list with **◀ ▶**. The filter () beside it narrows the list by text, participant, condition or annotation, and **⇅** sorts it. On a trial recorded over several screens, **Screen** picks the screen to draw. When several participants have the same trial ID, the list shows each reading with its participant in brackets, such as `3 [p2]`.

[All controls → Trial control bar](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/#trial-control-bar) describes each control.

## Control the layers

The **Plot controls** column, on the right of the plot, holds the figure's settings. Each layer has a row with a switch that turns it on or off and a **▾** that opens its settings.

| Section                  | What it controls                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Animate**              | replay the fixations in the order they happened, at a speed you choose                                                                   |
| **Compare**              | draw a second reading over this one, beside it or below it                                                                               |
| **Design presets**       | restyle the whole figure in one click: **Scanpath**, **Heatmap**, **Illustration**, or **Custom** for your most recent settings          |
| **My designs**           | save the current settings as a design, apply it again in one click, or export your designs to share them or use them on another computer |
| **Palette**              | one color scheme for the whole figure: **Default (colorblind-safe)**, **Print / grayscale** or **High contrast**                         |
| **Fixations**            | the fixation markers: color, shape and size, and the fixation index                                                                      |
| **Saccades**             | the saccade lines and arrows, in one color, by direction or by saccade type                                                              |
| **Stimulus**             | the text (or redacted blocks), highlighted words, the stimulus image, the font and the background                                        |
| **Word boxes**           | each word's box: outline and fill, color and opacity                                                                                     |
| **Heatmap**              | where fixations concentrate, by fixation count or duration                                                                               |
| **Raw gaze**             | the gaze samples as recorded                                                                                                             |
| **Filters & highlights** | which fixations and saccades are drawn, and which stand out                                                                              |
| **Figure & canvas**      | screen framing, axes and grid, title and labels, hover fields and legends                                                                |

[All controls → Plot controls](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/#plot-controls) describes every setting in each menu.

\[!\[

\](../../assets/workflows/plot-controls_poster.webp)\](../../assets/workflows/plot-controls.mp4)

## Under the plot

| Tab                    | What it is for                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Annotations**        | Star, tag and write notes on the trial, to find or filter it later.                                                                                                                                              |
| **Stimulus & context** | The trial's context, such as its title, question and answers, and its highlighted word spans.                                                                                                                    |
| **Comparisons**        | Show the other trials that share a field with this one, such as other readings of the same text, in a grid of small figures.                                                                                     |
| **Export**             | Download the figure on screen (PNG, SVG, PDF or HTML) or its replay (HTML, GIF or MP4), or build a zip bundle of figures and data for many trials.                                                               |
| **Share**              | **Link** reopens this trial with these settings for anyone who has the same dataset. **Code** gives the Python or CLI code that redraws the figure. **Settings file** saves the plot settings and restores them. |

[All controls → Under the plot](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/#under-the-plot) lists each tab's controls.

Watch the tabs under the figure

\[!\[

\](../../assets/workflows/subtabs_poster.webp)\](../../assets/workflows/subtabs.mp4)

## Render in code

Set up a figure in the app, then open **Share** → **Code** for the Python or CLI code that redraws it. For a dataset you imported, replace the placeholder file paths with your own.

Python and CLI: render the demo

```
import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
fig = sps.plot_scanpath(words, fixations, "l37_1129", "l37_1129_2_1_1_Ele")
sps.save_figure(fig, "scanpath.html")
```

```
scanpath-studio render --sample \
  -p l37_1129 -t l37_1129_2_1_1_Ele -o scanpath.html
```

For your own files, use the [data loaders](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/loading-data/#load-and-inspect-in-code). The [figure options table](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/api/#figure-options) lists every figure setting with its Python keyword and CLI flag. For more CLI examples, see [Common tasks](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/cli/#common-tasks).

The [gallery](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/gallery/index.md) shows how to make heatmaps, comparisons, replays and other figures in the app, the CLI and Python. For batch export and GIF or MP4 replays, see [Export and share](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/exporting/index.md).

## Back up your work

You can save each of these to a file and load it again:

| What                               | Where                                              |
| ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| figure settings                    | **Share** → **Settings file**                      |
| favorites, tags and notes          | **Data Management** → **Annotations** → **Export** |
| column mapping and recording setup | **Edit dataset** → **Download setup file**         |
| saved figure designs               | **My designs** → **Export**                        |

None of these files holds your data, so load the same data before you restore one. In the desktop app or a local install, the app also keeps your datasets, annotations and designs between sessions. See **Data Management** → **Saved on this computer**.

# All controls

Every control in the **Scanpath** view, where it is and what it does, in the order you meet them on screen. Search this page (`Ctrl`+`F`, or `Cmd`+`F` on a Mac) for the thing you want to change, such as *colors*, *legends* or *axes*.

The view has two sets of controls:

- The **trial control bar**, above the plot, decides *what* you see: the dataset, the trial, and which trials are in the list.
- The **plot controls**, the column on the right, decide *how* it is drawn: each layer of the figure, its colors and sizes, and the figure as a whole.

The tabs under the plot then work with the trial on screen: annotate it, read its context, compare it, export it or share it. For how the parts fit together, see the [Scanpath visualization](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/scanpath-visualization/index.md) guide.

For the corresponding Python keywords and CLI flags, use the [figure options table](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/api/#figure-options).

## Trial control bar

The bar above the plot: pick a dataset and a trial, step through the trials, and narrow, sort or label the list.

| Control                                           | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Select dataset**                                | The dataset the view shows.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| → **Draw a scanpath**                             | Write a text and place its fixations by hand, as a new dataset.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| → **Import files**                                | Upload your own Fixations and Words tables as a new dataset.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **Select trial**                                  | The trial to show. Click it and type to narrow the list.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Slider                                            | Move through the trials in the list.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| **◀ ▶**                                           | The previous or next trial.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **⇅** → **Sort trials by**                        | Reorder the trial list by a statistic (such as reading time), a participant, text or condition field, or a column of a metadata table you attached.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **⇅** → **Descending**                            | Reverse that order.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| → **Text** / **Participant**                      | Keep only these texts or participants. Empty keeps all.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| → *a field of your data*                          | Keep only trials with these values, or, for a number, in this range.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| → **By participant** / **By trial** / **By text** | The same, for the columns of an attached metadata table.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| → **Favorites only**                              | Keep only starred trials.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| → **With any of these tags**                      | Keep only trials with any of these tags.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| → **Excluding tags**                              | Hide trials with any of these tags, such as *To exclude*.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| → **✕ Clear all filters**                         | Reset every filter in the panel.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| → **Show the trial summary above the plot**       | Show or hide the row of facts about the trial above the plot.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| → field lists                                     | Drag fields between *Shown* and *Available* to choose the trial summary's fields, and drag within *Shown* to reorder them. *Available* holds every field with one value per trial: participant, text and condition columns, the columns of any metadata table you attached, and statistics such as reading time and fixation count. |
| → **Field colors**                                | Give a field a highlight color. Its **✕** puts it back to the default gray.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| → **Refresh fields**                              | Check again which fields have one value per trial.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Screen** and its **◀ ▶**                        | On a trial recorded over several screens: the screen to show.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

## Plot controls

The column on the right of the plot. At the top, the modes and designs change the whole figure at once. Under them, each layer of the figure has a row: the switch turns the layer on or off, and the **▾** beside it opens that layer's settings, described below one menu at a time. The last two rows, **Filters & highlights** and **Figure & canvas**, cover the figure as a whole. A grayed-out control says why when you hover over it.

### Animate: play the reading as a video

The **Animate** switch turns the figure into an animation, a video of the reading played back fixation by fixation, with play and pause buttons and a time slider above the plot. While it is on, the **Fixations**, **Heatmap** and **Raw gaze** switches are grayed. Its **▾** holds:

| Control                                 | What it does                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Replay** → **Speed**                  | How fast the video plays, from ×0.25 to ×8: ×1 is the participant's recorded pace, ×2 twice as fast, ×0.5 half as fast.                                                 |
| **Replay** → **Autoplay** → **On load** | Start playing the animation as soon as the plot is shown. Otherwise it starts when you click play.                                                                      |
| **Replay** → **Duration**               | For information only: the trial's reading time, and how long the video runs at this speed.                                                                              |
| **Frames** → **Quality**                | How smooth the video is: **Coarse**, **Standard** or **Fine**. More frames play more smoothly but take longer to build. Moving either slider below makes it **Custom**. |
| **Frames** → **Every**                  | Reading time between frames, in ms.                                                                                                                                     |
| **Frames** → **Limit**                  | The most frames a video gets. A long trial gets wider frame steps to fit.                                                                                               |
| **Frames** → **Result**                 | For information only: how many frames this trial's video has, and how far apart they ended up.                                                                          |

### Compare

The **Compare** switch shows a second scanpath, B, beside or over this one. Pick B in the [trial control bar](#trial-control-bar), above the plot. Its **▾** holds:

| Control                         | What it does                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **View**                        | **Overlay** both scanpaths, or give each a panel, **Side by side** or **Top & bottom**. With **Animate** on, the comparison is an overlay.                       |
| **Stimulus from**               | In an overlay, whose word boxes and text are drawn: **Both**, **A** or **B**.                                                                                    |
| **Label A** / **Label B**       | Each scanpath's name in the Compare (A/B) legend, written with fields such as `{participant_id}`. Empty uses the automatic label. Shown while that legend is on. |
| **Available fields**            | The fields a label can use.                                                                                                                                      |
| **Step** → **A and B together** | ◀ ▶ move both scanpaths at once.                                                                                                                                 |

### Design presets and palette

Restyle the whole figure in one click, with a ready-made design or one you saved:

| Control                                       | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Scanpath** / **Heatmap** / **Illustration** | Ready-made designs: fixations and saccades over the text, a word-box heatmap, or a clean schematic.                                                                                         |
| **Custom**                                    | Your most recent hand-made settings.                                                                                                                                                        |
| **My designs**                                | Your saved designs. Click one to apply it. renames it and deletes it.                                                                                                                       |
| **My designs** →                              | Save the settings on screen as a named design, to apply again later in one click.                                                                                                           |
| **My designs** → **Export** / **Import**      | Download your designs as a file, or load a file of designs, to share a look with co-authors or move your designs to another computer. A design in the file replaces yours of the same name. |
| **Palette**                                   | A color scheme for the whole figure: **Default (colorblind-safe)**, **Print / grayscale** or **High contrast**. It reads **Custom** once you change one of its colors.                      |

### Fixations

The **Fixations** switch draws the fixation markers. Its **▾** holds:

| Control                                                                                       | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Marker** → **Color**                                                                        | What decides each marker's color. **One color**, the default, paints them all alike. Pick a number column of the fixations, such as duration or time, and the markers follow a color scale: with the default blues, longer fixations show darker. Pick a category, such as **Text line** or a part-of-speech column, and each value gets a color, with a legend. |
| **Marker** → color box                                                                        | With **One color**: the fixation marker color. With a number column: the color scale.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **Marker** → **Range**                                                                        | When markers are colored by a number: the values at the two ends of the color scale. **Auto** fits each trial.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Marker** → **Shape**                                                                        | Choose the fixation marker shape: circle, square, diamond, triangle, cross, X, star, hexagon or heart.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **Marker** → **Size**                                                                         | Set the marker size range: the smallest and largest marker diameter, in px.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Marker** → **Scale**                                                                        | Choose how duration sets marker size: square root (the default), linear, log, or relative to this figure (its shortest to its longest fixation).                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **Marker** → **Durations**                                                                    | Set the durations (ms) that get the smallest and the largest marker. Not used on the relative scale.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **Marker** → **Opacity**                                                                      | Set the fixation marker opacity. Lower it to see overlapping fixations.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **Marker** → **Outline**                                                                      | Set the width (px) and color of the ring around each marker. A width of 0 draws none.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **Color bar** → **Show**                                                                      | Show the color scale's bar, when markers are colored by a number.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| **Color bar** → **Vertical** / **Horizontal**, **Angle**, **Size**, **Thickness**, **Length** | Set the bar's direction (right of the plot or below it), its tick-label angle and size, and its thickness and length.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **Fixation index** → **Show**                                                                 | Number each fixation in reading order.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **Fixation index** → color, **Size**                                                          | Choose the numbers' color and size.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **Snap** → **To line**                                                                        | Move each fixation up or down onto its line of text. This makes a schematic, labeled *Illustration*.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **Snap** → **Position**                                                                       | Choose where on its line a snapped fixation sits.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

### Saccades

The **Saccades** switch draws the lines between fixations. Its **▾** holds:

| Control                               | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Line** → **Color**                  | Choose what decides the saccade color: **One color** for all; **Forward / regression**, two colors; or **By type**, a color per saccade type (forward, skip, refixation, return sweep, regression), with a legend. **Forward / regression** and **By type** need a word ID for each fixation, the word it landed on, mapped as the Fixations table's **Word ID** (such as EyeLink's `CURRENT_FIX_INTEREST_AREA_ID`). Without one, every saccade is drawn as *Off the text*. |
| **Line** → color box                  | With **One color**: the saccade line color.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **Line** → **Types**                  | With **Forward / regression** or **By type**: the color of each group, such as regressions or return sweeps.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| **Line** → **Style**                  | Choose the saccade line style: solid, dashed, dotted or dash-dot.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **Line** → **Width**                  | Set the saccade line width (thickness), in px.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **Line** → **Opacity**                | Set the saccade line and arrow opacity. Lower it to bring the fixations forward.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **Shape**                             | Choose the saccade shape. **Straight** draws lines. **Arc** draws arcs over the text, a schematic labeled *Illustration*.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Direction arrows** → **Show**       | Show saccade direction arrows: an arrowhead on each saccade, pointing where the eye went.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Direction arrows** → **Arrow size** | Set the saccade arrowhead size.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

### Stimulus

The **Stimulus** switch draws the text and the stimulus image. The text rows start from the dataset's Recording setup, and changes here apply to the figure only. Its **▾** holds:

| Control                           | What it does                                                                                                                                                                              |
| --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Text** → **Show**               | Show the stimulus text, the words the participant read, at their place on the screen.                                                                                                     |
| **Text** → **Redact**             | Draw a rounded block over each word's letters instead of the word, in the text color, and hide the word in the hovers, so a figure shows where the text was without showing what it said. |
| **Fit** → **Fit to word boxes**   | Size the stimulus text from its word boxes, instead of a fixed font size.                                                                                                                 |
| **Fit** → **Spacing**             | With **Fit to word boxes** on: the distance between lines, in font sizes. The font size is that distance divided by this value, so 3 leaves a blank line above and below.                 |
| **Size**                          | With **Fit to word boxes** on: the size of the axis and legend text, in px. Off: the stimulus text's size too, in px or pt.                                                               |
| **Font**                          | Choose the stimulus text font (typeface). *Other font…* takes any font name.                                                                                                              |
| **Color** → text color            | Choose the stimulus text color.                                                                                                                                                           |
| **Color** → **Background**        | Choose the plot background color: a preset, or any color in the box beside it.                                                                                                            |
| **Highlight words** → **Show**    | Highlight words in the stimulus text, such as the answer span.                                                                                                                            |
| **Highlight words** → word column | Choose which words to highlight: a true/false word column, such as the critical span.                                                                                                     |
| **Style**                         | Choose the word highlight style, **Mark text** (colored text) or **Mark border** (a border around the words), and the highlight color.                                                    |
| **Image** → **Show**              | Show the stimulus image, the screen as shown in the experiment, under the scanpath.                                                                                                       |
| **File**                          | Upload a stimulus image (PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP) to draw under the scanpath. It replaces the dataset's image and is not included in Share links.                                          |
| **Opacity**                       | Set the stimulus image opacity. Lower it so the scanpath reads over it.                                                                                                                   |
| **Offset** → **X** / **Y**        | Move (nudge) the stimulus image left, right, up or down, in px, to line it up with the word boxes.                                                                                        |
| **Scale**                         | Resize (scale) the stimulus image so its text matches the word boxes.                                                                                                                     |

### Word boxes

The **Word boxes** switch draws each word's box (its interest area). Its **▾** holds:

| Control                    | What it does                                            |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Box** → **Line** color   | Choose the word box outline (border) color.             |
| **Box** → **Line** opacity | Set the word box outline opacity. 0 hides the outlines. |
| **Box** → **Fill** color   | Choose the word box fill color, inside each box.        |
| **Box** → **Fill** opacity | Set the word box fill opacity. 0 draws outlines only.   |

### Heatmap

The **Heatmap** switch shows where reading concentrated. Its **▾** holds:

| Control                                                                               | What it does                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Style**                                                                             | Choose the heatmap style: **Word boxes** colors each word box, **Smoothed** blurs the fixations with a Gaussian. Compare always uses word boxes.                 |
| **Blur**                                                                              | For **Smoothed**: how far each fixation spreads, in px. **Auto** picks it from the size of the data.                                                             |
| **Color** → **By**                                                                    | Choose what the heatmap measures: total fixation duration (dwell time), or **Fixation count**.                                                                   |
| **Color** → **Colors**                                                                | Choose the heatmap colors (color scale).                                                                                                                         |
| **Scale**                                                                             | Choose a linear or log heatmap scale.                                                                                                                            |
| **Range**                                                                             | For word-box heatmaps, fix the color range across trials. **Auto** runs from 0 to the trial's highest value. Smoothed heatmaps are scaled to each figure's peak. |
| **Opacity**                                                                           | Set the heatmap opacity. **Auto** uses 0.5 for word boxes and 0.45 for smoothed.                                                                                 |
| **Color bar** → **Show**, orientation, **Angle**, **Size**, **Thickness**, **Length** | Show the heatmap color bar, and set its orientation, label angle and size, thickness and length.                                                                 |

### Raw gaze

The **Raw gaze** switch draws the gaze samples as recorded. Its **▾** holds:

| Control                  | What it does                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Marker** → **Color**   | Not used outside Compare: the samples are colored by their time, or by their order when they have no timestamps. |
| **Marker** → **Size**    | Set the raw gaze sample marker size.                                                                             |
| **Marker** → **Opacity** | Set the raw gaze sample opacity.                                                                                 |

### Filters & highlights

Which fixations and saccades are drawn, and which stand out:

| Control                         | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
