| `--dpi`                 | `N`                     | —       | Resolution of `--width-mm` / `--width-in` (default: 300).                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `--separable-layers`    | switch                  | —       | Also write one file per layer (word boxes, fixations, saccades, heatmap, labels, stimulus image) to a `&lt;output&gt;_layers/` folder, to restyle each in Illustrator or Inkscape. The layers line up when stacked. Static image output only: .svg, .pdf or .png. |
| `--print-code`          | `python`, `cli`, `both` | —       | Print the Python or CLI code that reproduces this figure (python, cli or both), then render as usual. The code sets only the options that differ from the defaults.                                                                                               |
| `--print-code-explicit` | switch                  | —       | With `--print-code`: write every figure option, including the ones at their defaults.                                                                                                                                                                             |

### Compare

| Option                                   | Value                                | Default     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--compare-with`                         | `PARTICIPANT:TRIAL`                  | —           | The second scanpath, B, as PARTICIPANT:TRIAL. It comes from the loaded dataset unless `--compare-words` / `--compare-fixations` load a second one.                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `--compare-screen`                       | `SCREEN_ID`                          | —           | B's screen in a multipart trial, looked up in B's trial (default: its first screen). `--screen` picks A's. Each scanpath is drawn from one screen.                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `--compare-layout`                       | `overlay`, `side-by-side`, `stacked` | `overlay`   | How A and B are arranged (default: overlay). Across two datasets, overlay needs canvases of the same size. Different canvases are refused, so use side-by-side or stacked for them. Matching canvases that a dataset did not record still overlay, with a warning.                                                                        |
| `--compare-stimulus`                     | `both`, `a`, `b`                     | `both`      | On an overlay, whose word boxes and text to draw (default: both). Two datasets' word boxes line up only when the text is the same.                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `--label-a`                              | `TEXT`                               | —           | Name of scanpath A in the legend and hovers. Used by the comparison and by `--animate`. Needs `--label-b`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `--label-b`                              | `TEXT`                               | —           | Name of scanpath B in the legend and hovers. Needs `--label-a`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `--compare-legend` `--no-compare-legend` | switch                               | —           | Draw the Compare (A/B) legend, which names the two scanpaths. On by default; `--no-compare-legend` hides it. Also applies to `--animate`.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `--style-a`                              | `SPEC`                               | —           | Style for scanpath A, repeatable: KEY=VALUE[,...]. Colors (#RRGGBB): fix_color, saccade_color, box_color (word-box outline; default fix_color), box_fill_color (default `--word-box-fill-color`), raw_gaze_color (default fix_color). Also heatmap_colorscale (default `--heatmap-colorscale`, on the shared range), saccade_style (solid |
| `--style-b`                              | `SPEC`                               | —           | Style for scanpath B, repeatable: KEY=VALUE[,...]. Colors (#RRGGBB): fix_color, saccade_color, box_color (word-box outline; default fix_color), box_fill_color (default `--word-box-fill-color`), raw_gaze_color (default fix_color). Also heatmap_colorscale (default `--heatmap-colorscale`, on the shared range), saccade_style (solid |
| `--compare-fixation-flag`                | `SPEC`                               | —           | Filters & highlights for scanpath B only. Repeatable. Same SPEC as `--fixation-flag`, e.g. `--compare-fixation-flag` short=hide,threshold_ms=80. Replaces `--fixation-flag` for B.                                                                                                                                                        |
| `--compare-saccade-classes`              | `CLASSES`                            | —           | The saccade types scanpath B draws, comma-separated, named as in `--saccade-classes`. Replaces `--saccade-classes` for B. Not with `--animate`, which draws every type.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `--compare-fix-index-range`              | `START:END`                          | —           | Draw only fixations START to END of scanpath B, counting from 1, both included. Replaces `--fix-index-range` for B.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `--stimulus-image-b`                     | `PATH`                               | —           | Scanpath B's stimulus image, for a side-by-side or stacked comparison across two datasets, where each panel draws its image. Sized and placed like `--stimulus-image`.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `--stimulus-image-size-b`                | `WxH`                                | —           | Size of `--stimulus-image-b` in px (default: the PNG's pixel size, else `--compare-canvas`, else `--canvas`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `--stimulus-image-origin-b`              | `X,Y`                                | —           | Top-left corner of `--stimulus-image-b` in B's screen px (default: 0,0).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `--compare-words`                        | `PATH [PATH ...]`                    | —           | The Words table for a second dataset, B's. Same formats and globbing as `--words`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `--compare-fixations`                    | `PATH [PATH ...]`                    | —           | The Fixations table for a second dataset, B's. Same formats and globbing as `--fixations`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `--compare-raw-gaze`                     | `PATH [PATH ...]`                    | —           | The Raw gaze table for the second dataset, drawn under B's scanpath. Same formats as `--raw-gaze`. With no second dataset, `--raw-gaze` already covers both scanpaths.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `--compare-dataset-name`                 | `NAME`                               | `Dataset B` | Name of the second dataset, used in the trace names (default: 'Dataset B').                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `--compare-canvas`                       | `WxH`                                | —           | The second dataset's screen size in px, e.g. 1680x1050. Estimated from its data when left out. An overlay, or `--animate` with both scanpaths, checks it against `--canvas`.                                                                                                                                                              |

## corpus

`corpus` renders a styled corpus figure from a tidy CSV you already have, as plot_corpus_figure does. For `--kind profile` the CSV needs `word_id` and `value` columns.

```
scanpath-studio corpus --input profile.csv --kind profile --output profile.svg
```

| Option              | Value                                   | Default   | Description                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------- | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--input`           | `PATH`                                  | required  | The CSV. profile reads word_id and the value column, plus optional lo and hi; distribution reads the value column; difference reads word_id and diff. |
| `--kind`            | `profile`, `distribution`, `difference` | required  | A per-word profile, a distribution, or a difference profile.                                                                                          |
| `-o` `--output`     | `PATH`                                  | required  | Output file; any extension save_figure writes (.html, .png, .svg, .pdf).                                                                              |
| `--measure-label`   | `MEASURE_LABEL`                         | `Value`   | Axis and legend label for the value (default: Value).                                                                                                 |
| `--series-col`      | `SERIES_COL`                            | `series`  | Column naming the overlaid series, when present (default: series).                                                                                    |
| `--value-col`       | `VALUE_COL`                             | `value`   | The value column (default: value).                                                                                                                    |
| `--primary-color`   | `PRIMARY_COLOR`                         | `#1f77b4` | First series color (default: #1f77b4).                                                                                                                |
| `--secondary-color` | `SECONDARY_COLOR`                       | `#e45756` | Second series color (default: #e45756).                                                                                                               |

## check

`check` runs the **Data Management** page's **Data checks** on your tables without opening the app. It looks for:

- fixations lasting 0 ms or less, or with an infinite duration or onset;
- fixations and raw gaze samples with no finite position, or one more than a million pixels off the screen;
- word boxes with no area, or no finite position or size within a million pixels;
- screen sizes that are not finite and positive.

Each finding gives the rows and trials affected, a few example rows, and what the app does with them. `check` changes nothing and exits 0 whatever it finds. `--json` prints the table check_data_health returns.

```
scanpath-studio check --words ia.csv --fixations fixations.csv
scanpath-studio check --raw-gaze gaze_samples.csv --json
```

| Option                   | Value                 | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------ | --------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--sample`               | switch                | —       | Check the bundled demo instead of your own tables.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `--words`                | `PATH [PATH ...]`     | —       | Words table(s), as for render.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `--fixations`            | `PATH [PATH ...]`     | —       | Fixations table(s), as for render.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `--raw-gaze`             | `PATH [PATH ...]`     | —       | The Raw gaze table, as for render.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `--raw-gaze-schema`      | `JSON`                | —       | Column mapping for the `--raw-gaze` table, replacing auto-detection, in the form `--fix-schema` takes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `--trial-parts-manifest` | `PATH`                | —       | JSON manifest assigning source rows to ordered screens.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `--json`                 | switch                | —       | Print the findings as JSON (the rows api.check_data_health returns).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `--word-schema`          | `JSON`                | —       | Column mapping for the `--words` table, replacing auto-detection. A JSON object from each field to a column name, or the path of a JSON file holding one, e.g. '{"trial": "TRIAL_INDEX", "word_id": "IA_ID", ...}'. It is the dict api.load_scanpath_data takes. Needed only when a column isn't recognized, and the error then prints a mapping to start from.     |
| `--fix-schema`           | `JSON`                | —       | Column mapping for the `--fixations` table, replacing auto-detection. A JSON object from each field to a column name, or the path of a JSON file holding one, e.g. '{"trial": "TRIAL_INDEX", "word_id": "IA_ID", ...}'. It is the dict api.load_scanpath_data takes. Needed only when a column isn't recognized, and the error then prints a mapping to start from. |
| `--keep-columns`         | `COLUMN [COLUMN ...]` | —       | More columns to keep through loading, under the names they have in your files (e.g. a pupil size), from whichever table has them. Without it, loading keeps only the mapped and recognized fields. A kept fixation column can be used by `--color-by`, an axis or a hover. Same as keep_columns= in api.load_scanpath_data.                                         |

## cache

A local or desktop run saves your session on your computer, so a refresh or a restart resumes where you left off. It saves uploaded datasets, column mappings, view settings, saved designs, metadata tables and annotations. `cache` shows what is stored and can delete it.

```
scanpath-studio cache            # datasets, rows, size, folder, last written
scanpath-studio cache --path     # just the folder
scanpath-studio cache --json     # the same status as JSON
scanpath-studio cache --clear    # delete the recovery cache
```

| Option    | Value  | Default | Description                      |
| --------- | ------ | ------- | -------------------------------- |
| `--path`  | switch | —       | Print the cache folder and exit. |
| `--json`  | switch | —       | Print the status as JSON.        |
| `--clear` | switch | —       | Delete the recovery cache.       |

The same information is at the foot of the **Data Management** page, under **Saved on this computer**. A running app writes a new copy at its next change, so clear the cache with the app closed.

| To                                       | Use                            |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| turn caching off for one launch          | `scanpath-studio --no-persist` |
| turn it off wherever the variable is set | `SCANPATH_STUDIO_PERSIST=0`    |
| move the folder                          | `SCANPATH_STUDIO_STATE_DIR`    |

Hosted deployments do not cache by default.

## version

`version` says which build this is and how it was installed. `--check` also asks GitHub whether a newer release is out and says how to update your install. Only `--check` uses the network.

```
scanpath-studio version           # the build, and how it was installed
scanpath-studio version --check   # …and whether a newer release is out
```

| Option      | Value     | Default | Description                                                           |
| ----------- | --------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--check`   | switch    | —       | Ask GitHub for the latest release and say how to update this install. |
| `--timeout` | `SECONDS` | `5.0`   | How long to wait for GitHub, in seconds (default: 5).                 |

Between releases the version names the build: `0.35.0.post3+g8f18219` is three commits after 0.35.0, at commit `8f18219`. The same check is **Help → About → Check for updates** in the app, and check_for_updates in Python.

# Across the experiment

Mean total fixation duration per word across one participant’s trials in the bundled demo. Each point is one trial. The bundled demo holds only part of the session.

1. Open your data in the **Corpus Analysis** view, on the **Per participant** tab.
1. Choose a participant, and in **View** choose **Per-trial trend**.
1. Choose a reading measure your data provides, and **Mean** in **Aggregate**. The horizontal axis is the trial order from the data’s `trial_index` or `TRIAL_INDEX` column. Without one, the app orders the trials by fixation time, or as listed.

[Follow the progression tutorial](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/tutorials/corpus-analysis/progression-over-time/index.md)

The corpus CLI does not offer trial-order trends. Download the [Python recipe](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/gallery/across-experiment/across-experiment.py) and run:

```
python across-experiment.py
```

This uses the app’s aggregation and trend builder.

```
import scanpath_studio as sps

from scanpath_studio.aggregation import metric_by_trial_index
from scanpath_studio.data import derive_trial_index
from scanpath_studio.plots import make_trend_figure

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data(names="canonical")
reader = words[words["participant_id"] == "l37_1129"].copy()
reader["trial_index"] = derive_trial_index(reader)
trend = metric_by_trial_index(reader, "total_fixation_duration_ms")
fig = make_trend_figure(
    trend,
    x_col="trial_index",
    x_label="Recorded trial order",
    y_label="Mean total fixation duration per word (ms)",
    title="Across the experiment · Participant A",
    canvas_width=1000,
    base_font_size=18,
    font_family="Arial",
    height=450,
    break_gaps=True,
)

sps.save_figure(fig, "across-experiment.html")
```

[← All examples](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/gallery/index.md)

# Two participants

Two complete readings of a shorter text, labeled Participant A and Participant B.

1. Open your data in the **Scanpath** view and pick a trial in **Select trial**.
1. Turn on **Compare**. In **Trial B**, choose another participant's reading of the same text.
1. In **Compare** ▾, set **View** to **Overlay**, and name the two readings in **Label A** and **Label B**. To compare the complete readings, keep the **Index range** of both scanpaths at the full range, under **Filters & highlights** ▾ → **Fixations · A** and **Fixations · B**.
1. In **Figure & canvas** ▾ → **Screen & framing**, tick **Frame** → **Crop to data**. Untick **Margin** → **Auto** and enter 50 px.
1. Under **Legends**, set **Compare (A/B)** to **Top center, outside** and **Side by side**, with text size 24. Untick **Show** for **Fixation sizes**.

[Open the demo](https://scanpath-studio.streamlit.app) · [All controls](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/index.md)

```
scanpath-studio render --sample \
  -p l37_1129 -t l37_1129_2_2_4_Ele \
  --compare-with l7_1090:l7_1090_2_2_4_Ele --compare-legend --label-a "Participant A" --label-b "Participant B" \
  --legend compare=top-center-outside,side-by-side,24 --no-duration-size-legend \
  --crop-to-data --crop-margin 50 \
  --highlight-column '' \
  -o comparison.html
```

```
import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
pid, tid = "l37_1129", "l37_1129_2_2_4_Ele"
fig = sps.compare_scanpaths(
    words,
    fixations,
    (pid, tid),
    ("l7_1090", "l7_1090_2_2_4_Ele"),
    labels=("Participant A", "Participant B"),
    fit_to_monitor=False,
    crop_margin=50,
    show_legend=True,
    duration_size_legend=False,
    legend_layout={
        "compare": {
            "position": "top-center-outside",
            "arrangement": "side-by-side",
            "size": 24,
        }
    },
)

sps.save_figure(fig, "comparison.html")
```

[← All examples](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/gallery/index.md)

# Fully customizable

Make a figure for a talk or teaching: pink hearts for fixations, purple arrows for the eye’s movements. This hand-drawn illustration follows The → cat → sat → on → the → mat, with one fixation per word.

1. Load your Words and Fixations tables, or the example [words](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/gallery/hearts-arrows/words.csv) and [fixations](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/gallery/hearts-arrows/fixations.csv). For the example, set **Recording setup** → **Screen** to **I know it**, 450 × 300 px. Open the dataset in the **Scanpath** view and pick a trial in **Select trial**.
1. In **Fixations** ▾ → **Marker**, set **Shape** to **♥ Heart**. Keep **Color** at **One color** and set its box to `#d12d72`. Set **Size** to **18–30** and **Opacity** to **0.85**. Tick **Snap** → **To line**, and leave **Fixation index** → **Show** unticked.
1. In **Saccades** ▾, set **Shape** to **Arc**. Under **Line**, keep **Color** at **One color** with `#4f46a5`, and set **Width** to **2.5**. Tick **Direction arrows** and set **Arrow size** to **12**.
1. In **Figure & canvas** ▾ → **Legends**, untick **Show** for **Fixation sizes**. Under **Title & labels** → **Illustration**, enter “Illustration · hand-drawn” in **Text**. Leave **Stimulus** ▾ → **Highlight words** unticked.

Save the look under **My designs** to apply it to your own data.

[Open the demo](https://scanpath-studio.streamlit.app) · [All controls](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/index.md)

Download the example [words](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/gallery/hearts-arrows/words.csv) and [fixations](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/gallery/hearts-arrows/fixations.csv) into the same folder.

```
scanpath-studio render --words words.csv --fixations fixations.csv \
  -p synthetic -t synthetic_2line_demo --canvas 450x300 \
  --fixation-symbol heart --fixation-color '#d12d72' \
  --marker-size-range 18 30 --fixation-opacity 0.85 --snap-fixations \
  --saccade-arcs --saccade-arrows --saccade-color '#4f46a5' \
  --saccade-width 2.5 --saccade-arrow-size 12 \
  --no-fixation-index --no-duration-size-legend --highlight-column '' \
  --illustration-text "Illustration · hand-drawn" -o hearts-arrows.html
```

```
import scanpath_studio as sps

from scanpath_studio.synthetic import make_synthetic_words

words = make_synthetic_words()
fixations = words[["participant_id", "trial_id", "text_id", "word_id"]].copy()
fixations["x"] = words["x"] + words["width"] / 2
fixations["y"] = words["y"] + words["height"] / 2
fixations["duration_ms"] = [100, 150, 120, 200, 90, 110]
fixations["timestamp_ms"] = (
    fixations["duration_ms"].cumsum() - fixations["duration_ms"]
)
fixations["order_in_trial"] = range(1, len(fixations) + 1)
fixations["pass_index"] = 1
pid, tid = "synthetic", "synthetic_2line_demo"
fig = sps.plot_scanpath(
    words,
    fixations,
    pid,
    tid,
    canvas_size=(450, 300),
    fixation_symbol="heart",
    fixation_color="#d12d72",
    marker_size_range=(18, 30),
    fixation_opacity=0.85,
    fixation_snap_to_line=True,
    saccade_render_mode="Arc",
    show_saccade_arrows=True,
    saccade_color="#4f46a5",
    saccade_width=2.5,
    saccade_arrow_size=12,
    show_order=False,
    duration_size_legend=False,
    illustration_text="Illustration · hand-drawn",
)

sps.save_figure(fig, "hearts-arrows.html")
```

[← All examples](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/gallery/index.md)

# Heatmap

Where fixation time concentrates.

1. Open your data in the **Scanpath** view and pick a trial in **Select trial**.
1. Turn on **Heatmap**. In **Heatmap** ▾ → **Style**, choose **Smoothed**. Keep **Color** → **By** at **Duration (ms)**.
1. Turn off **Fixations** and **Saccades**, and keep **Stimulus** on.

[Open the demo](https://scanpath-studio.streamlit.app) · [All controls](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/index.md)

```
scanpath-studio render --sample \
  -p l37_1129 -t l37_1129_2_1_1_Ele \
  --heatmap --heatmap-style smoothed --no-fixations --no-saccades \
  --highlight-column '' \
  -o heatmap.html
```

```
import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
pid, tid = "l37_1129", "l37_1129_2_1_1_Ele"
fig = sps.plot_scanpath(
    words,
    fixations,
    pid,
    tid,
    show_heatmap=True,
    heatmap_style="Smoothed",
    show_fixations=False,
    show_saccades=False,
)

sps.save_figure(fig, "heatmap.html")
```

[← All examples](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/gallery/index.md)

# Highlighted text

Highlight a selected text span alongside its fixations.

1. Load a Words table with a true/false column that marks the words to highlight, and your Fixations table. Open the dataset in the **Scanpath** view and pick a trial in **Select trial**.
1. In **Stimulus** ▾, tick **Highlight words** and choose that column.
1. Under **Style**, keep **Mark text** and pick the highlight color in the box beside it. To show only the highlighted text and the fixations, turn off **Saccades**.

[Open the demo](https://scanpath-studio.streamlit.app) · [All controls](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/index.md)

```
scanpath-studio render --sample \
  -p l37_1129 -t l37_1129_2_1_1_Ele \
  --highlight-column is_in_aspan --critical-span-style mark-text \
  --no-saccades -o highlighted-text.html
```

```
import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
pid, tid = "l37_1129", "l37_1129_2_1_1_Ele"
fig = sps.plot_scanpath(
    words,
    fixations,
    pid,
    tid,
    highlight_column="is_in_aspan",
    critical_span_style="Mark text",
    show_saccades=False,
)

sps.save_figure(fig, "highlighted-text.html")
```

# Reading schematic

A hand-drawn two-line text, with one fixation per word in reading order: The → cat → sat → on → the → mat. Fixations sit on the lines and saccades are arcs.

1. Load your Words and Fixations tables, or the example [words](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/gallery/illustration/words.csv) and [fixations](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/gallery/illustration/fixations.csv). For the example, set **Recording setup** → **Screen** to **I know it**, 450 × 340 px.
1. Open the dataset in the **Scanpath** view and pick a trial in **Select trial**.
1. In **Fixations** ▾, tick **Snap** → **To line** and **Fixation index** → **Show**. In **Saccades** ▾ → **Shape**, choose **Arc**.
1. In **Figure & canvas** ▾ → **Legends**, untick **Show** for **Fixation sizes**. Under **Title & labels** → **Illustration**, enter “Illustration · hand-drawn” in **Text**.

[Open the demo](https://scanpath-studio.streamlit.app) · [All controls](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/index.md)

Download the example [words](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/gallery/illustration/words.csv) and [fixations](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/gallery/illustration/fixations.csv) into the same folder.

```
scanpath-studio render --words words.csv --fixations fixations.csv \
  -p synthetic -t synthetic_2line_demo \
  --canvas 450x340 --snap-fixations --saccade-arcs --fixation-index \
  --illustration-text "Illustration · hand-drawn" --no-duration-size-legend \
  --highlight-column '' -o illustration.html
```

```
import scanpath_studio as sps

from scanpath_studio.synthetic import make_synthetic_words

words = make_synthetic_words()
fixations = words[["participant_id", "trial_id", "text_id", "word_id"]].copy()
fixations["x"] = words["x"] + words["width"] / 2
fixations["y"] = words["y"] + words["height"] / 2
fixations["duration_ms"] = [100, 150, 120, 200, 90, 110]
fixations["timestamp_ms"] = (
    fixations["duration_ms"].cumsum() - fixations["duration_ms"]
)
fixations["order_in_trial"] = range(1, len(fixations) + 1)
fixations["pass_index"] = 1
pid, tid = "synthetic", "synthetic_2line_demo"
fig = sps.plot_scanpath(
    words,
    fixations,
    pid,
    tid,
    canvas_size=(450, 340),
    fixation_snap_to_line=True,
    saccade_render_mode="Arc",
    illustration_text="Illustration · hand-drawn",
    show_order=True,
    duration_size_legend=False,
)

sps.save_figure(fig, "illustration.html")
```

[← All examples](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/gallery/index.md)

# Raw gaze

Gaze samples under translucent fixations. The bundled demo's gaze samples are synthetic.

1. Load a Raw gaze table with your Fixations and Words tables. Open the dataset in the **Scanpath** view and pick a trial in **Select trial**.
1. Turn on **Raw gaze** and turn off **Saccades**.
1. In **Fixations** ▾ → **Marker** → **Opacity**, set 0.35 so the samples show through.

[Open the demo](https://scanpath-studio.streamlit.app) · [All controls](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/index.md)

```
scanpath-studio render --sample \
  -p l37_1129 -t l37_1129_2_2_2_Adv \
  --sample-raw-gaze --fixation-opacity 0.35 --no-saccades \
  --highlight-column '' \
  -o raw-gaze.html
```

```
import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
pid, tid = "l37_1129", "l37_1129_2_1_1_Ele"
raw_gaze = sps.load_sample_raw_gaze()
fig = sps.plot_scanpath(
    words,
    fixations,
    "l37_1129",
    "l37_1129_2_2_2_Adv",
    raw_gaze=raw_gaze,
    fixation_opacity=0.35,
    show_saccades=False,
)

sps.save_figure(fig, "raw-gaze.html")
```

[← All examples](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/gallery/index.md)

# Redacted text

Show where the text was without showing what it said. Each word is drawn as a rounded block over its letters, and the hovers hide the words too.

1. Open your data in the **Scanpath** view and pick a trial in **Select trial**.
1. In **Stimulus** ▾ → **Text**, tick **Redact**. The blocks take the text color.

[Open the demo](https://scanpath-studio.streamlit.app) · [All controls](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/index.md)

```
scanpath-studio render --sample \
  -p l37_1129 -t l37_1129_2_1_1_Ele \
  --redact-text --highlight-column '' \
  -o redacted-text.html
```

```
import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
pid, tid = "l37_1129", "l37_1129_2_1_1_Ele"
fig = sps.plot_scanpath(words, fixations, pid, tid, redact_text=True)

sps.save_figure(fig, "redacted-text.html")
```

[← All examples](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/gallery/index.md)

# Replay

Replay a reading in fixation order. Press **▶ Play** above the text to start this example, **⏸ Pause** to stop, or drag the time slider to inspect a moment. The example shows the first forty fixations at twice the recorded speed.

1. Open your data in the **Scanpath** view and pick a trial in **Select trial**.
1. Turn on **Animate**. To replay part of the reading, set **Filters & highlights** ▾ → **Fixations** → **Index range**, here 1 to 40.
1. In **Animate** ▾ → **Replay** → **Speed**, choose **×2**, then press **▶ Play** above the plot. Use **⏸ Pause** or the time slider to inspect the reading.
1. Save the replay from **Export** → **Current figure**.

[Open the demo](https://scanpath-studio.streamlit.app) · [All controls](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/index.md)

```
scanpath-studio render --sample \
  -p l37_1129 -t l37_1129_2_1_1_Ele \
  --animate --fix-index-range 1:40 --playback-speed 2 \
  --highlight-column '' \
  -o replay.html
```

```
import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
pid, tid = "l37_1129", "l37_1129_2_1_1_Ele"
fig = sps.animate_scanpath(
    words,
    fixations,
    pid,
    tid,
    fix_index_range=(1, 40),
    playback_speed=2.0,
)

sps.save_figure(fig, "replay.html")
```

[← All examples](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/gallery/index.md)

# Saccade types

Forward movements, skips, refixations, return sweeps and regressions.

ForwardSkipRefixationReturn sweepRegressionOff the text

1. Open your data in the **Scanpath** view and pick a trial in **Select trial**.
1. In **Saccades** ▾ → **Line** → **Color**, choose **By type**.
1. To match this example, open **Figure & canvas** ▾ → **Legends** and untick **Show** for **Saccade types**. This page shows the color key below the figure.

[Open the demo](https://scanpath-studio.streamlit.app) · [All controls](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/index.md)

```
scanpath-studio render --sample \
  -p l37_1129 -t l37_1129_2_1_1_Ele \
  --saccade-color-by-type --no-saccade-type-legend \
  --highlight-column '' \
  -o saccade-types.html
```

```
import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
pid, tid = "l37_1129", "l37_1129_2_1_1_Ele"
fig = sps.plot_scanpath(
    words,
    fixations,
    pid,
    tid,
    saccade_color_mode="By type",
    saccade_type_legend=False,
)

sps.save_figure(fig, "saccade-types.html")
```

# Scanpath

Fixations and saccades over the text.

1. Open your data in the **Scanpath** view and pick a trial in **Select trial**.
1. In **Design presets**, click **Scanpath**. It turns on **Fixations**, **Saccades** and **Stimulus**.
1. Save the figure from **Export** → **Current figure**.

[Open the demo](https://scanpath-studio.streamlit.app) · [All controls](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/index.md)

```
scanpath-studio render --sample \
  -p l37_1129 -t l37_1129_2_1_1_Ele \
  --highlight-column '' \
  -o scanpath.html
```

```
import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
pid, tid = "l37_1129", "l37_1129_2_1_1_Ele"
fig = sps.plot_scanpath(words, fixations, pid, tid)

sps.save_figure(fig, "scanpath.html")
```

# Fixations by line

Fixations colored by their nearest text line.

1. Open your data in the **Scanpath** view and pick a trial in **Select trial**.
1. In **Fixations** ▾ → **Marker** → **Color**, choose **Text line (computed)**.
1. Keep **Saccades** and **Stimulus** on. Each fixation takes the color of the nearest line of word boxes.

[Open the demo](https://scanpath-studio.streamlit.app) · [All controls](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/index.md)

```
scanpath-studio render --sample \
  -p l37_1129 -t l37_1129_2_1_1_Ele \
  --color-by-line \
  --highlight-column '' \
  -o text-lines.html
```

```
import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
pid, tid = "l37_1129", "l37_1129_2_1_1_Ele"
fig = sps.plot_scanpath(words, fixations, pid, tid, color_by_line=True)

sps.save_figure(fig, "text-lines.html")
```

[← All examples](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/gallery/index.md)

# Title, caption & legend

A figure ready for a slide or a paper. It has a title above the plot, a caption below it, the **Saccade types** legend down the right side and the **Fixation sizes** legend below the plot.

1. Open your data in the **Scanpath** view and pick a trial in **Select trial**.
1. In **Saccades** ▾ → **Line** → **Color**, choose **By type**.
1. In **Figure & canvas** ▾ → **Title & labels**, tick **Title** and **Caption**. Enter a title for your reading and a caption that explains the markers and colors. Set each one's **Size**, here 34 px and 20 px.
1. Under **Legends**, set **Saccade types** to **Right, outside** and **Fixation sizes** to **Bottom right, outside**, both with text size 18.
1. Under **Screen & framing**, tick **Frame** → **Crop to data**. Untick **Margin** → **Auto** and enter 60 px.

[Open the demo](https://scanpath-studio.streamlit.app) · [All controls](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/index.md)

```
scanpath-studio render --sample \
  -p l37_1129 -t l37_1129_2_1_1_Ele \
  --saccade-color-by-type \
  --title "One participant, one article" --title-size 34 \
  --caption "Marker size: fixation duration. Line color: saccade type." --caption-size 20 \
  --legend saccades=right-outside,,18 --legend size-key=bottom-right-outside,,18 \
  --crop-to-data --crop-margin 60 \
  --highlight-column '' \
  -o title-caption-legend.html
```

```
import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
pid, tid = "l37_1129", "l37_1129_2_1_1_Ele"
fig = sps.plot_scanpath(
    words,
    fixations,
    pid,
    tid,
    saccade_color_mode="By type",
    title="One participant, one article",
    title_font_size=34,
    caption="Marker size: fixation duration. Line color: saccade type.",
    caption_font_size=20,
    legend_layout={
        "saccades": {"position": "right-outside", "size": 18},
        "size_key": {"position": "bottom-right-outside", "size": 18},
    },
    fit_to_monitor=False,
    crop_margin=60,
)

sps.save_figure(fig, "title-caption-legend.html")
```

[← All examples](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/gallery/index.md)

# Word-box heatmap

Fixation time within each word box.

1. Open your data in the **Scanpath** view and pick a trial in **Select trial**.
1. Turn on **Heatmap**. In **Heatmap** ▾ → **Style**, choose **Word boxes**. Keep **Color** → **By** at **Duration (ms)**.
1. Turn off **Fixations** and **Saccades**, and keep **Stimulus** on.

[Open the demo](https://scanpath-studio.streamlit.app) · [All controls](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/index.md)

```
scanpath-studio render --sample \
  -p l37_1129 -t l37_1129_2_1_1_Ele \
  --heatmap --heatmap-style word-boxes --no-fixations --no-saccades \
  --highlight-column '' \
  -o word-boxes.html
```

```
import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
pid, tid = "l37_1129", "l37_1129_2_1_1_Ele"
fig = sps.plot_scanpath(
    words,
    fixations,
    pid,
    tid,
    show_heatmap=True,
    heatmap_style="Word boxes",
    show_fixations=False,
    show_saccades=False,
)

sps.save_figure(fig, "word-boxes.html")
```

# About Scanpath Studio

**Scanpath Studio v0.42.1** — interactive visualization of eye movements in reading.

Developed by [Omer Shubi](https://omershubi.github.io/), [Keren Gruteke Klein](https://kerengruteke.github.io/), [Maya Grossman](https://www.linkedin.com/in/maya-grossman-32b547292/), [Ella Lion](https://ella-lion.github.io/), [Deborah N. Jakobi](https://www.cl.uzh.ch/en/research-groups/digital-linguistics/people/lab-members/jakobi.html), [David R. Reich](https://www.cl.uzh.ch/en/research-groups/digital-linguistics/people/lab-members/reich.html), [Lena Jäger](https://www.cl.uzh.ch/en/research-groups/digital-linguistics/people/group-leader/jaeger.html), and [Yevgeni Berzak](https://dds.technion.ac.il/people/academic-staff/yevgeni-berzak/), at the Technion and the University of Zurich.

## Bundled demo

The bundled demo is a subset of **OneStop Eye Movements**. If you use it, also cite Berzak et al. (2025), *OneStop: A 360-Participant English Eye Tracking Dataset with Different Reading Regimes*, Scientific Data. [DOI: 10.1038/s41597-025-06272-2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-025-06272-2).

## Privacy

With the desktop app or a local install, your recordings stay on your computer and are processed locally. The online demo processes the files you upload on its hosted server. **Help** → **About** says which of the two you are using.

### Your data

A local install (`scanpath-studio`) and the desktop app save your work on your computer, so a refresh or a restart picks up where you left off.

- **What is saved:** the datasets you added, with their column mappings, your annotations, your saved designs, attached metadata tables, and your view, trial and plot settings. The bundled demo and public datasets are not copied, since they reload from their source.
- **Where:** `~/.cache/scanpath-studio/session-v1` in your home folder (`C:\Users\<you>\.cache\scanpath-studio\session-v1` on Windows), or the folder `SCANPATH_STUDIO_STATE_DIR` names. **Data Management** → **Saved on this computer** shows the folder and what it holds, and so does `scanpath-studio cache`.
- **How long:** until you clear it. Removing a dataset from the app removes its saved copy.
- **To clear it:** **Clear what is saved…** under **Saved on this computer**, or close the app and run `scanpath-studio cache --clear`.
- **To turn it off:** start the app with `scanpath-studio --no-persist`, or set `SCANPATH_STUDIO_PERSIST=0`.

The online demo saves nothing. A file you upload there is processed on Streamlit Community Cloud and not kept, so closing or refreshing the tab loses it. The app itself has no analytics, but Community Cloud's page around the app does; see its [privacy policy](https://streamlit.io/privacy-policy). Export your annotations and settings before you leave ([what to back up](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/guides/scanpath-visualization/#back-up-your-work)).

## Questions and feedback

[Ask a question](https://github.com/lacclab/scanpath-studio/discussions/categories/q-a), [report a bug](https://github.com/lacclab/scanpath-studio/issues/new?template=bug_report.md), or [request a feature](https://github.com/lacclab/scanpath-studio/issues/new?template=feature_request.md). For a bug report, include the version, your operating system and how you run the app. The app shows its version in **Help** → **About**.

Developed with AI assistance. Cross-check results before publishing.
